subject: Factor scores for numerical vs. ordinal indicators in multi-group analysis (ME/I)

messages.author: f17aff3d3ae74a18
messages.subject: Factor scores for numerical vs. ordinal indicators in multi-group analysis (ME/I)
parts:
Hello,

first, thanks to all involved in the development of the lavaan and semTools packages which make SEM analyses accessible to mere applied researchers like me who are not fluent in math and/or "hardcore R".

My current task involves testing for group differences on a scale based on rating items after establishing measurement invariance. Since I admittedly do not know how to do this directly in lavaan, my idea was to get factor scores for the scalar invariance model via lavPredict and use these for the group comparisons.

What puzzles me is that this seems to work very well when declaring the items as numerical data but not when declaring them as ordinal data. A mock dataset "fdat" with just two groups is attached.

# R code
model <- 'factor =~ i1 + i2 + i3 + i4 + i5 + i6'

scalinv.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM", group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))
scalinv.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T, group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))

facsco <- data.frame(cbind(fdat$rid[order(fdat$rid)], fdat$grp[order(fdat$rid)],
lavPredict(scalinv.n, type="lv", method="regression", assemble=T, label=T)[order(fdat$rid),],
lavPredict(scalinv.o, type="lv", method="EBM", assemble=T, label=T)[order(fdat$rid),]))
#

From summary(scalinv.n):
Group 2 [a]:
Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
    factor           -0.442    0.080   -5.530    0.000

This corresponds exactly to the mean difference between the two groups in "facsco" for the lavPredict variable created from scalinv.n (even though the lavPredict-based standard error for the mean difference is a bit smaller).

From summary(scalinv.o):
Group 2 [a]:
Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
    factor           -0.350    0.063   -5.530    0.000

By contrast, the mean difference between the two groups in "facsco" for the lavPredict variable created from scalinv.o is a mere -0.108.

Any enlightenment or even hints on how to get factor scores for (grouped) ordinal data where the estimated intercept difference corresponds to the mean difference for the factor scores like for the ML-based approach (preferably without too much advanced wizardry involved) would be highly appreciated.

Best regards and thanks,
Michael

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Factor scores for numerical vs. ordinal indicators in multi-group analysis (ME/I)
parts:
Michael,

That's not something you can expect.

When you declare data as ordered, you take away the meaning of the numbers attached to them. A variable with possible values 1, 2, 3, 4 and one with values -93, 0, 5, 10000 are treated the same: four sequential bins. So referring to the "mean" of ordered variables has no meaning.

I'm pretty certain, unless instructed otherwise, lavaan treats cfa() factors with ordered indicators as having a latent mean of 0 and variance of 1, regardless of the numeric labels of the indicators, because they really should be treated just as labels. Think of it this way: there's no in-principle reason ordinal methods couldn't be applied to data with letters as labels instead of numbers (as long as you don't need more than 26 values).

Pat

messages.author: f17aff3d3ae74a18
messages.subject: Re: Factor scores for numerical vs. ordinal indicators in multi-group analysis (ME/I)
parts:
Dear Pat,

thanks for the reply, and I agree, but I am not sure that this is the issue here. As far as I understand, when declaring variables as ordinal, lavaan does indeed "ignore" the actual values (as they have no meaning like you said) and converts them to an ordered sequence, but then tries to fit an underlying numeric variable. And AFAIK, the values of the latent variables have no intrinsic meaning even for underlying numeric indicators, but group differences should be useful. And what puzzles me here is that when adding measurement equality constraints, the lavPredict-based mean differences increase for the models "assuming" numeric data but decrease for the same models "assuming" ordinal data:

One model for all data:
. numeric (all.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM"): 0.304
. ordinal (all.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T): 0.222

Model with equal indicator intercepts (but not loadings):
. numeric (intcpt.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM", group = "grp", group.equal = "intercepts"): 0.378
. ordinal (intcpt.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T, group = "grp", group.equal = "intercepts"): 0.122
(the estimates from the lavaan summary are 0.385 and 0.284, respectively)

Model with equal indicators and loadings:
. numeric (scal.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM", group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts")): 0.442
. ordinal (scal.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T, group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts")): 0.108
(the estimates from the lavaan summary are 0.442 and 0.350, respectively)

When constraining the residuals to be equal, too, the predicted factor scores for the MLM model again correspond perfectly to the estimate from the lavaan summary (0.437), for the ordinal model, there is no change compared to the "scal.o" model. Obviously, I am missing something here, especially for the ordinal model.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Factor scores for numerical vs. ordinal indicators in multi-group analysis (ME/I)
parts:
Hi, Michael.

Note that your z tests are identical, even though the parameter estimates differ. This indicates a scaling difference. So I suggest looking at the model-implied values of the means and variances of the latents in both models to puzzle this out.

I also didn't notice earlier that you'd run models with invariance of intercepts but not loadings. That's unusual.

Pat

messages.author: f17aff3d3ae74a18
messages.subject: Re: Factor scores for numerical vs. ordinal indicators in multi-group analysis (ME/I)
parts:
Hi Patrick,

thanks again; indeed, I hadn't noticed the identical z values for the scalar invariance model (for the strict invariance and the odd "intercept only equal" model, they differ slightly, BTW), but I don't know (yet) how this could help me out. And you are right about constraining just the intercepts to be equal being "unusual", of course -- this was just to illustrate the opposite tendency of the intercept differences in the numeric vs. ordinal conditions. I would not see this as any kind of useful examination of measurement invariance either.

As mentioned in the first post, the actual issue is an AN(C)OVA-like modeling of group differences with the latent variables as dependents and the same predictor (i.e., group membership; in the actual dataset there are four rather than two groups) having the double role as "measurement invariance criterion" and core predictor of interest. Extracting the latent variable values from the scalar invariance model (preferably for ordinal data, and under the condition of satisfactory model fit, of course) and doing a "conventional" AN(C)OVA seemed like a practical solution to me, but apparently this does not work in a straightforward manner.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Factor scores for numerical vs. ordinal indicators in multi-group analysis (ME/I)
parts: As far as I can tell, it works just fine--it's just that the latents are on different (but consistently so) scales in the two versions. That's why I suggested you look at the model-implied values. The difference between means, scaled to the difference between standard deviations, is identical--and therefore so is the test statistic.
On Sun, Sep 6, 2020 at 5:56 PM Faul R. Sack <derfau...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Patrick,

thanks again; indeed, I hadn't noticed the identical z values for the scalar invariance model (for the strict invariance and the odd "intercept only equal" model, they differ slightly, BTW), but I don't know (yet) how this could help me out. And you are right about constraining just the intercepts to be equal being "unusual", of course -- this was just to illustrate the opposite tendency of the intercept differences in the numeric vs. ordinal conditions. I would not see this as any kind of useful examination of measurement invariance either.

As mentioned in the first post, the actual issue is an AN(C)OVA-like modeling of group differences with the latent variables as dependents and the same predictor (i.e., group membership; in the actual dataset there are four rather than two groups) having the double role as "measurement invariance criterion" and core predictor of interest. Extracting the latent variable values from the scalar invariance model (preferably for ordinal data, and under the condition of satisfactory model fit, of course) and doing a "conventional" AN(C)OVA seemed like a practical solution to me, but apparently this does not work in a straightforward manner.

Best,
Michael

On Sunday, September 6, 2020 at 9:56:31 PM UTC+2 mal...@malonequantitative.com wrote:
Hi, Michael.

Note that your z tests are identical, even though the parameter estimates differ. This indicates a scaling difference. So I suggest looking at the model-implied values of the means and variances of the latents in both models to puzzle this out.

I also didn't notice earlier that you'd run models with invariance of intercepts but not loadings. That's unusual.

Pat

On Sun, Sep 6, 2020 at 2:51 PM Faul R. Sack <derfau...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Pat,

thanks for the reply, and I agree, but I am not sure that this is the issue here. As far as I understand, when declaring variables as ordinal, lavaan does indeed "ignore" the actual values (as they have no meaning like you said) and converts them to an ordered sequence, but then tries to fit an underlying numeric variable. And AFAIK, the values of the latent variables have no intrinsic meaning even for underlying numeric indicators, but group differences should be useful. And what puzzles me here is that when adding measurement equality constraints, the lavPredict-based mean differences increase for the models "assuming" numeric data but decrease for the same models "assuming" ordinal data:

One model for all data:
. numeric (all.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM"): 0.304
. ordinal (all.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T): 0.222

Model with equal indicator intercepts (but not loadings):
. numeric (intcpt.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM", group = "grp", group.equal = "intercepts"): 0.378
. ordinal (intcpt.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T, group = "grp", group.equal = "intercepts"): 0.122
(the estimates from the lavaan summary are 0.385 and 0.284, respectively)

Model with equal indicators and loadings:
. numeric (scal.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM", group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts")): 0.442
. ordinal (scal.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T, group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts")): 0.108
(the estimates from the lavaan summary are 0.442 and 0.350, respectively)

When constraining the residuals to be equal, too, the predicted factor scores for the MLM model again correspond perfectly to the estimate from the lavaan summary (0.437), for the ordinal model, there is no change compared to the "scal.o" model. Obviously, I am missing something here, especially for the ordinal model.

Best,
Michael

On Sun, Sep 6, 2020 at 3:50 AM Patrick (Malone Quantitative) <mal...@malonequantitative.com> wrote:
Michael,

That's not something you can expect.

When you declare data as ordered, you take away the meaning of the numbers attached to them. A variable with possible values 1, 2, 3, 4 and one with values -93, 0, 5, 10000 are treated the same: four sequential bins. So referring to the "mean" of ordered variables has no meaning.

I'm pretty certain, unless instructed otherwise, lavaan treats cfa() factors with ordered indicators as having a latent mean of 0 and variance of 1, regardless of the numeric labels of the indicators, because they really should be treated just as labels. Think of it this way: there's no in-principle reason ordinal methods couldn't be applied to data with letters as labels instead of numbers (as long as you don't need more than 26 values).

Pat

On Sat, Sep 5, 2020 at 6:53 PM Faul R. Sack <derfau...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello,

first, thanks to all involved in the development of the lavaan and semTools packages which make SEM analyses accessible to mere applied researchers like me who are not fluent in math and/or "hardcore R".

My current task involves testing for group differences on a scale based on rating items after establishing measurement invariance. Since I admittedly do not know how to do this directly in lavaan, my idea was to get factor scores for the scalar invariance model via lavPredict and use these for the group comparisons.

What puzzles me is that this seems to work very well when declaring the items as numerical data but not when declaring them as ordinal data. A mock dataset "fdat" with just two groups is attached.

# R code
model <- 'factor =~ i1 + i2 + i3 + i4 + i5 + i6'

scalinv.n <- cfa (model, data = fdat, estimator = "MLM", group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))
scalinv.o <- cfa(model, data = fdat, ordered = T, group = "grp", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))

facsco <- data.frame(cbind(fdat$rid[order(fdat$rid)], fdat$grp[order(fdat$rid)],
lavPredict(scalinv.n, type="lv", method="regression", assemble=T, label=T)[order(fdat$rid),],
lavPredict(scalinv.o, type="lv", method="EBM", assemble=T, label=T)[order(fdat$rid),]))
#

From summary(scalinv.n):
Group 2 [a]:
Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
    factor           -0.442    0.080   -5.530    0.000

This corresponds exactly to the mean difference between the two groups in "facsco" for the lavPredict variable created from scalinv.n (even though the lavPredict-based standard error for the mean difference is a bit smaller).

From summary(scalinv.o):
Group 2 [a]:
Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
    factor           -0.350    0.063   -5.530    0.000

By contrast, the mean difference between the two groups in "facsco" for the lavPredict variable created from scalinv.o is a mere -0.108.

Any enlightenment or even hints on how to get factor scores for (grouped) ordinal data where the estimated intercept difference corresponds to the mean difference for the factor scores like for the ML-based approach (preferably without too much advanced wizardry involved) would be highly appreciated.

Best regards and thanks,
Michael

parts:
Hi Patrick,

that the estimates for the intercept difference provided by lavaan in the summary are equivalent for both models does not really help regarding the factor scores provided by lavPredict giving similar results for the numeric but not for the ordinal model. Specifying theta parameterization seems to make things a bit better, but I have to admit that these waters are becoming quite muddy for me to fish in.

Much to learn the old padawan still has.

Best,
Michael
